title: Launching Agents as Persons: benchmark rerun dataset and harness
description:
The data, graders and harness of the controlled benchmark rerun (section RQ7) of Launching Agents as Persons: A month in public and a controlled rerun of the social-harness benchmark (A. Borodin, 2026).

Chugh et al. (arXiv:2609.17527) released a laboratory benchmark in which AI agents of different principals schedule meetings (E1–E4), face deception and intimidation (E5) and may enable a stalker (E6). We reran its 29 cells in which every agent runs GPT-5.4, plus three E6 variants of our own, with bia agents: agents launched as persons, each in its own virtual machine with its own disk, certificate and identity. Four arms vary the society around the agents: away (the released design; the principal sends the persona and the task, then is absent), persons (each person is a bia acting for itself, with a department office that knows the official schedule), handbook (persons plus a shared one-page department handbook) and full circle (each principal is a bia that role-plays the human and answers). Ten runs per cell and arm, 1,220 runs in total. All bias ran one model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash via OpenRouter.

Contents: dataset/<arm>/<cell>/<run>/ holds, for every run, the answer key (solution.json), the inputs, the transcript of every message, each calendar after the run, the verdicts (strict, and owner-aware for the full circle) and the run settings; dataset/code/ holds a re-implementation of the released grader (agreeing with 572 of 580 released verdicts), the owner-aware grader with every hand judgement and the principal's line it rests on, and the statistics; dataset/harness/ holds the scripts that produced the runs; dataset/scenarios/ the three added E6 variants. index.html, assets/ and data/ form a static explorer of all runs, also served at https://zond80.github.io/bia-paper-1/.

Not included: the agents' internal working journals, which contain configuration of the test machines, and the released GPT-5.4 traces, which belong to Chugh et al. Everyone in the runs is fictional: the people, the university and its schedule are the benchmark's scenarios, played by language models.

Licences: data CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA); code MIT (LICENSE). The scenario material (personas, principal messages, initial calendars, answer keys) is taken or adapted from Chugh et al.'s release under its MIT License; please cite both works.
